coreLogic: Two-branch calculation: (1) schedule path — if a schedule is resolved, calls BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours($date, $this->getGracePeriod(), $timeline) in include/class.schedule.php (lines 475-485), which instantiates new BusinessHours($schedule) and calls BusinessHours::addWorkingHours($date, $hours) in include/class.businesshours.php (starting line 87) — this walks the schedule's business-hours entries/holidays, mutates $date's timezone to the schedule's zone, accumulates working seconds until the requested grace hours are met (backtracking with DateTime::sub if it overshoots), and returns false if the schedule has zero entries; on success $timeline is set from $bhrs->getTimeline() and the mutated $date is returned. (2) fallback path — reached when no schedule resolves OR addWorkingHours() returns false: $time = round($this->getGracePeriod()*3600); $date->add(new DateInterval('PT'.$time.'S')); return $date.
consumers: Ticket::getSLADueDate() in include/class.ticket.php (lines 547-563) — resolves $schedule = $this->getDept()->getSchedule(), builds $dt from getReopenDate()/getCreateDate() in the DB timezone, calls $dt = $sla->addGracePeriod($dt, $schedule), converts $dt back to the DB timezone, and returns $dt->format('Y-m-d H:i:s'). Downstream callers of getSLADueDate(): Ticket::updateEstDueDate() persists the result as $this->est_duedate, and Ticket::getEstDueDate() falls back to it when no hard due date is set.
inputShape: $date: DateTime instance, mutated in place and also returned (advance point for the grace period). $schedule: optional BusinessHoursSchedule, nullable — an explicitly requested schedule that overrides the SLA's own. $timeline: optional array passed by reference, populated with BusinessHours audit-log entries only when the schedule path succeeds. Implicit inputs read from object/global state: $this->getGracePeriod() (SLA's grace_period field, in hours), $this->getSchedule() (SLA's own schedule via schedule_id, lazily loaded), global $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (system default schedule, lazily loaded).
outputShape: Returns the same DateTime instance passed as $date, advanced in place by the grace period — either via the business-hours-aware path (schedule resolved and has entries) or a flat DateInterval of round(gracePeriodHours*3600) seconds (fallback path). No new DateTime is constructed; callers rely on both the return value and the in-place mutation of $date. The by-reference $timeline argument is populated only on the successful schedule path.
sideEffects: Reads global $cfg to call $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() as the last fallback in schedule precedence resolution.
SLA::getSchedule() lazily loads and memoizes $this->_schedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) — a DB read cached on the SLA instance.
Config::getDefaultSchedule() lazily loads and memoizes $cfg->defaultSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($cfg->getDefaultScheduleId()) — a DB read cached on the config instance.

BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours() constructs a new BusinessHours($schedule) object each call and invokes its addWorkingHours(), which reads schedule entries and holiday schedules off the Schedule object (DB-backed lazy-loaded properties) and builds an internal audit timeline via BusinessHours::timeline()/getTimeline().

Mutates the caller-supplied $date DateTime in place: setTimezone() to the schedule's DateTimeZone on the schedule path, plus DateInterval add()/sub() operations on both the schedule and fallback paths.
Mutates the by-reference $timeline argument (only on the successful schedule path).
No direct SQL writes occur in this method or its delegation chain; all side effects are reads/lazy-caching plus in-place mutation of $date and $timeline.
constraints: Schedule precedence is fixed and order-sensitive: explicitly passed $schedule argument > SLA's own schedule ($this->getSchedule()) > system default ($cfg->getDefaultSchedule()), using an ?: short-circuit chain where the first truthy value wins.
If a schedule resolves to non-null AND BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours() succeeds (returns the DateTime, not false), that result is returned immediately and the fallback path must not execute.

If no schedule resolves (all three precedence sources falsy) OR addWorkingHours() returns false (e.g. the resolved schedule has zero business-hours entries), execution falls through to the flat wall-clock addition: round(gracePeriodHours * 3600) seconds via DateInterval('PT{n}S').

Grace period hours always come from $this->getGracePeriod() (the SLA instance's own grace_period field) on both paths — never from the $schedule argument's own configuration — even though a different schedule object may be supplied by the caller.
$timeline is populated only on the successful schedule path; on the fallback path it retains whatever value the caller passed in (defaults to an empty array).

Method signature (Datetime $date, BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null, &$timeline = array()) and the return contract (same DateTime instance, advanced in place) must be unchanged after extraction — callers keep working identically.

Timezone handling differs by branch: the schedule path forces $date's timezone to the schedule's DateTimeZone before computing; the fallback path performs no timezone change and adds the interval in $date's existing timezone. This distinction must be preserved exactly.

Extracted service must never call back into SLA::addGracePeriod() (anti-recursion). It should perform forward delegation to BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours()/BusinessHours (or lift the inline fallback DateInterval expression), while include/class.sla.php retains the $cfg/global schedule-precedence orchestration and simply calls the service with an already-resolved schedule (or null) plus the grace-period hours.
